trait.name: Rise Again
entries: If Josh is killed permanently or brought below 0 hit points, he does not enter death saving throws. Instead, he will rise again with full hit points within 1 hour, unless he is still pierced by a wooden or silver weapon.

contents.name: The Passion of The Heist
headers: What Am I Reading Right Now?
How Do I Use This Module

data.name: The Passion of The Heist

entries: *But when they looked in the tomb, they found that it was empty. And when they looked in the vault, they found that it too was empty, and that all the riches had been removed. For Joshua and his disciples had in fact pulled off the sickest heist that had ever been seen, and all were in awe of their triumph.*
— Remorans 13:1

Along the coast of the White Sea, where the mighty Remoran empire stretches into the eastern marches, a messiah speaks the word of the Lord, providing hope and solace to the conquered peoples of the land. During his constant travels he has picked up a number of disciples, who join him in his miraculous deeds. Your players are these disciples, among others.

While most of their time with Joshua has been spent caring for the poor and protecting the weak, sometimes a few colored eggs must be broken if one is to make an omelette. As the party settles in for one final dinner, their leader lays the plans for a great heist that will target the Remoran Empire itself. All it will require of them is to die and rise again.

entries.name: What Am I Reading Right Now?
entries: This is a Dungeons and Dragons 5th Ed. homebrew adventure in which the resurrection of Christ is retold as a heist movie. It is a one-shot adventure made to be played in 1–3 sittings. It should take somewhere between 4 and 6 hours. As written, everything should be balanced for a 4 player party of level 5 adventurers, however there is considerable flexibility given the open nature of the module.

entries.name: How Do I Use This Module
entries: This document will provide an overview of the main story points and the locations your players may find themselves in for this adventure. In particular this module is broken into five parts.

items: Background Info: Everything you need to know before beginning the story.
Opening: How to begin the adventure and introduce all your player characters.
The Heist Part 1: The first section of the heist that will largely follow a linear progression.
The Heist Part 2: The second and much longer section of the heist that can be approached in many ways.
Conclusion: The ending to the story.

entries: {@b Bolded} words refer to items, maps, or non-playable characters (NPCs) whose information can be found outside of the main text. When your players come across new items, information will be included in info boxes near the relevant section. However, in the interest of space, maps and stat blocks for NPCs are included at the end of this document rather than interspersed within the text.

entries.name: Judrael
entries: Judrael is a province in the Remoran Empire, conquered from the local peoples roughly 100 years prior to this adventure. The capital is Shalem, where this adventure will take place, and the governor is {@creature Pontius Pilate|PassionOfTheHeist}. Although the Remorans worship a variety of different gods, the locals primarily worship the Demiurge, a being depicted as a snake with the head of a lion.

entries.name: The Apostles
entries: Your players, among others, have been disciples of Joshua, a local prophet, for some time now. Perhaps it has been many months, perhaps several years. They do not need to model themselves after the apostles in the Bible, nor do they need to have a particularly religion-based class or backstory. They do, however, need to be genuine followers of Joshua and his god, the one true god, the Monad, or the One. Likely they joined him after hearing of his great deeds throughout the land.
The apostles who accompany Joshua but are not player characters use the {@creature Generic Apostle|PassionOfTheHeist} stat block.

entries.name: Joshua
entries: {@creature Josh|PassionOfTheHeist}, in his own words, is the son of God. Not just any god, but the most powerful of all gods, the Monad, the One, the Totality of All. He appears as a man in his thirties, wearing plain clothes and a beard. To add to his humble demeanor, he typically refers to be addressed as Josh, especially by his followers.

Although his good deeds have done a great deal to help the people of Judrael, he has also made a number of enemies in the region. Many in the Remoran administration view the community he has fostered with increasing suspicion. Many of the more devout worshipers of the Demiurge are apprehensive about his rival god.

entries.name: Messiah Powers
entries: As the ostensible son of God, Josh has an array of powers that he has used in his travels. At will, he can turn water into wine, walk on water, and heal curses and afflictions. He can also heal the party's hit points when they take damage during the heist. Up to 4 times, Josh can lay his hands on a creature to heal {@damage 2d8 + 5} hit points.

entries.name: Josh's Secret
entries: {@b Do not give this information to your players! They should discover it slowly on their own.} Although the true nature of Josh's godly ancestry will remain ambiguous, his powers in fact come from a source different from the Monad. Josh is in fact a vampire, albeit a subtle one. Several clues should be dropped throughout the adventure

items: Josh has unusually pale skin for the region. This should only be mentioned in passing, but it can also be used as a joke about western depictions of Jesus.
Although the players will have to be given a potion to fake their deaths, Josh will not. He will mention he hopes he doesn't get any splinters, however.
Josh will speak to the bats in the caves to help the party navigate. He will insist that it's just a son of God thing.
Josh has a penchant for counting, and if faced with many small objects in his path, he will have to count them or come up with an excuse not to proceed.
Josh can fly, and he can also climb along walls and ceilings.
Josh does not have a reflection.
Josh laughs with a distinct ah ah ah! But not very loudly.
Josh has an innate spider climb ability, and will often use this to perch upside down on the ceiling while avoiding the guards.
Josh points out that by entombing the party in the hill, the Remorans are technically inviting them into the treasury.
If the party is in desperate straits and likely to lose on their own, Josh will reveal his fangs and attack. Ideally this will not happen until the climax of the adventure.

entries.name: NPC & Enemy Stat Blocks
entries: This adventure includes stat blocks for most of the NPCs your characters may find themselves engaging in combat with. Note that enemies have been given higher damage and lower health in order to make encounters short but deadly. Overall, the relative strength of your players and their enemies should still be balanced, depending on how many they engage at once. However, it is possible that this set-up will favor certain character builds over others.

entries.name: Introduction
entries: To set the scene, read the following paragraph, or paraphrase in a way that suits your style.

This story begins in the capital of Judrael, Shalem. It is a relic of an older time, with ancient temples and statues throughout, but also a symbol of Remoran power, with soldiers stationed on the streets, and newly constructed behemoths sticking out like sore thumbs made of white marble pillars. The blue banner of the empire hangs from every civil building, reminding the conquered people who their masters are.

We find ourselves in a small tavern, The Grey Goose, where a celebration is taking place. There are [12 - #players] people sitting on one side of the table, their leader, Josh, in the center. Several guests are joining us now.
Players will then introduce their characters by having them enter the tavern one by one. As they step inside they are greeted by Josh and the other apostles, who beckon them over to join them.

entries.name: The Final Dinner
entries: Josh and his apostles are celebrating Crossover, as are a few other groups present in the tavern. All good friends, they are drinking and laughing and generally having a good time. Across the room, a halfling named Craig is playing the lute, performing a collection of songs he calls {@i Lofi Beats to Study/Eat Your Last Meal To}.

Standing in the middle of the room, a Tortle named Leo is trying to paint everyone, attempting in vain to get everyone to hold still. This, of course, is why everyone is sitting on the same side of the table. Though convenient for the painting, the tavern owner is less amused, complaining about empty seats. Apparently they had a group just the previous night that wanted to do the same thing, all these messiahs and their dramatic meetings. Though

Before giving his speech, Josh is trying to get his hands on some bread and wine to use as props. The best he is able to acquire is a large baguette and some pink lemonade, which don't work quite as well.

entries.name: Josh's Speech
entries: After the players have gotten a chance to introduce themselves and see everything going on, Josh will open his speech by trying to use the baguette and pink lemonade as metaphors. While he holds it up, he inevitably keeps hitting people with the baguette, and is eventually forced to give up.

Deciding to cut to the chase, Josh tells Craig the lute player to switch to a more dramatic tune, setting the tone as he tells everyone why he's brought them here today. They are going to rob the Remoran Empire, and he has a plan to do it.

entries.name: The Plan
entries: The Remoran Public Treasury, located on the edges of Shalem, contains a vault holding unimaginable wealth, which the Remorans use to fund their armies in the area. There is only one entrance to the treasury, and it has the highest security in all of the known realms. Trying to enter through this way means almost certain death. Which is exactly why they are going to avoid this entrance entirely.

The treasury is built into a hill, on the side opposite to where the tombs are located. Since some of the tombs contain Remoran citizens, the tombs themselves are also heavily guarded, {@i but only from the outside}. Josh's plan is to set up himself and several apostles in order to be executed, fake their own deaths, and once entombed tunnel to the back of the treasury.

Josh has a mole in the Remoran guard who will help them to do this. While they are on the crosses, he will offer them {@i Fool's Nightshade}, a wine that makes people appear dead for several hours. Joshua will not need this wine, instead just using his own powers as the son of God.

Remoran law allows all buried by the state to be entombed with their belongings, which will allow them to bring in their weapons and other useful objects. First however, they must all drink from the {@b Potion of Forgetability}, which Josh now offers to the party.

entries.name: Potion of Forgetability
entries: {@item Potion of Forgetability|PassionOfTheHeist}

entries.name: The Arrest
entries: The final question is how exactly they are going to get themselves convicted and executed. Josh informs the group that one of them has betrayed him, and if so, everything is going according to plan. In fact the apostle Judah confirms that he has informed the authorities, giving them a tip on several miscreants committing blasphemy and treason. Right on cue, several {@creature Remoran Soldier|PassionOfTheHeist|Remoran Soldiers} kick down the door. They look much like Roman soldiers, except their color is blue rather than red and they are wearing metallic masks as part of their helmets modeled after honored ancestors. The soldiers arrest all of the players as well as Josh. The remaining apostles have not been arrested, as their job is to make sure all the weapons and items are entombed with the heisters.

data.name: 3. The Heist Part 1
entries: The party's goal for this segment of the heist is to be convicted, crucified, and then placed in the tombs. From there they will attempt to tunnel their way to the Remoran Treasury.

entries.name: The Trial
entries: After some time, we cut to the party being led to the edge of a fenced-in courtyard, just in front of a massive building made of fine marble and sporting an excessive number of pillars. There is a crowd outside the gates cheering with ambiguous loyalties. Many are dressed in sports jerseys and probably got confused on their way to the local Rootball match. Either way, the energy is palpable.

On a balcony overhead stands {@creature Pontius Pilate|PassionOfTheHeist}, the Remoran governor, along with several advisors and additional {@creature Remoran Soldier|PassionOfTheHeist|Remoran Soldiers}. A balcony to his left hold various local officials, who only seem to be present for administrative reasons. To his right are the high priests of the Demiurge, wearing emblems of the snake with the lion's head and flanked by their {@creature Elite Aarakocra Bodyguard|PassionOfTheHeist|elite aarakocra bodyguards}. Their leader, an older woman in fine robes, stands at the front with an unamused expression.

A podium stands in the middle of the courtyard with an elven lawyer waiting to help with their defense. This is unfortunate, because defense is exactly what they are not looking for. Josh demonstrates this first as proceeds to cuss out everyone present, saying that he's the son of God, that he's better than all of them, and that they don't know anything. The lawyer is taken aback by this and will grow increasingly stressed as his clients intentionally get themselves convicted.
After Josh, each player will be brought up to the podium and must make everyone angry enough to convict them. In particular they must anger three groups.

entries.name: The High Priests
entries: The high priests do not in fact represent the locals of Judrael but were supplanted by the Castilucian Inquisition in order to gain influence in the region. As such, they represent a much more extreme position and wish to exert their religious control over all affairs. This is all to say that they won't need much encouragement to convict the players, who have been accused of blasphemy.

entries.name: The Crowd
entries: The crowd is easily swayed and easily confused. They do not have the same resentment for the party's heresy as the high priests, but are eager to see something exciting happen. They are likely to get hung up on stupid stuff and make nonsensical demands, many still thinking this is the Rootball match.

entries.name: Pontius Pilate
entries: Pilate truly does not understand what the big deal is, or what crimes Josh and the players have actually committed. He will be the hardest of them all to convince, and is more likely to just give up than actually convict the party with malice. When he does, he will likely question the need to crucify them at all. It seems very dramatic, doesn't it? Why don't they just give them the hemlock? The high priests and the crowd, if sufficiently riled up, will not find this acceptable and will insist on crucifixion.

At some point, Pilate will offer to free one of two prisoners: the player on trial, or Abba McKillin, an enormous man with a massive beard who grumbles about how much he loves killing. The crowd will choose McKillin, much to Pilate's chagrin.

Since there is only one outcome that will move the story forward, it is best to resolve this section through role playing rather than some kind of skill challenge. If your party are not very big on roleplaying in this way, the trial can be sped up by having all players and Josh tried at the same time.

entries.name: The Crucifixion
entries: Some more time passes and we cut to the party riding over to the edge of the city in a prison carriage. Following the contingent of soldiers on horseback are the remaining disciples, who follow on donkeys carrying the party's weapons and items. The carriage stops in front of the crosses that have already been set up. A few yards away is the hill containing the tombs, guarded by another contingent of {@creature Remoran Soldier|PassionOfTheHeist|Remoran Soldiers}.

The soldiers place wooden buckets in front of the crosses and somewhat awkwardly tell the party to get up and be crucified. Each player must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw to avoid {@damage 2d4} piercing damage as they are nailed to the cross. Josh does not appear to be in much pain, but he does comment that he's worried about splinters.

Most of the soldiers then wander off and "leave them to it" until the party has died. One {@creature Remoran Soldier|PassionOfTheHeist}, Morgan, reveals themselves as the mole working for Josh. Morgan is really having fun with the covert spy stuff and doesn't really appreciate the immense pain the party is experiencing. Eventually though, she gives them the Fool's Nightshade through a straw made of reeds, with Josh insisting he doesn't need it, and that he's more worried about sunburn than dying up there. All of them pass out of consciousness in a matter of seconds.

entries.name: The Tomb
entries: The party wakes up inside a small tomb, unsure how long they have been in there. A magical light hovers in the air, illuminating all there is around them. Josh is sitting against the wall, bored, counting the pebbles on the ground to pass the time. He is quite happy to see that the players are up, and indicates to the weapons and {@area Starting Items|3.4|x} lying around them.

After using the {@item Olive Branches of Dousing|PassionOfTheHeist} to locate the cave tunnels, a {@dc 14} Strength check is required to break down the wall, else the {@item Holy Pocket Shark|PassionOfTheHeist} or one of the players' spells must be used up instead.

entries.name: Starting Items
entries: {@item Gloves of Spider-Climb|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Trampoline of Turin|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Olive Branches of Dousing|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Rabbit Slippers|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Breathing Bubble|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Ring of the Second Dimension|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Magic Banana|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Ring of Boneless Chicken|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Cheep Cheep Egg|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Lantern of Silence|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Cross of Inattention|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Egg Potion (2 Uses)|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Holy Pocket Shark|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Basket of Holding (X5)|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Crown of Thorns|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Portal Spyglass|PassionOfTheHeist}

entries.name: The Caves
entries: As they climb out of their personal tomb and deeper into the hillside, the party is faced with a treacherous system of tunnels, often too narrow to stand up in, and often requiring them to move in a single file. As they pass through a particularly dark and narrow section, the players must each succeed on a {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check in order to avoid getting separated from the party. When they do, they will have to face one of the challenges below randomly determined by a d4. Everyone who does not get lost will face the remaining challenges together.

entries.name: 1. The Tomb
entries: The player arrives at the end of a tunnel to reach a small room carved out of stone with a coffin propped against the back wall. Several {@area Tomb Items|3.5|x} lay scattered across the floor along with broken pottery and other debris. When the player steps far enough into the room, a {@creature Mummy (Tomb)|PassionOfTheHeist} will jump out to attack them.

entries.name: Tomb Items
entries: {@item Ring of Making It Rain|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Ancient Sword|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Size Serum|PassionOfTheHeist}

entries.name: 2. The Flooded Tomb
entries: The player comes across a crumbling room that has been flooded, the water at least a few feet deep. At first it seems rather pleasant. A hole in the stone above opens to a vibrant ray of light from the sky, and a small group of baby ducks are sitting idle in the water. Floating in an old chest are the {@area Flooded Tomb Items|3.6|x}. But if a player attempts to open the chest, the {@creature Drowned Mummy|PassionOfTheHeist} will emerge from the water and try to pull them in.

entries.name: Flooded Tomb Items
entries: {@item Ring of Healing All Your Health|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Grappling Bow|PassionOfTheHeist}

entries.name: 3. The Empty Tomb
entries: The player arrives at a relatively clean and well-carved room. This tomb is empty save for the treasure chest located against the opposite wall. Inside this chest is in fact a trap that will shoot sharp spikes out when opened. A {@dc 11} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check is required if the player wants to discern if there is anything wrong with the chest. Otherwise, they must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw to avoid take {@damage 2d6} piercing damage. Inside the chest they will find the {@item Burning Bush Branch|PassionOfTheHeist}.

entries.name: Empty Tomb Items
entries: {@item Burning Bush Branch|PassionOfTheHeist}

entries.name: 4. The Earthworm
entries: While crouching through a narrow tunnel, the player comes across a {@creature Giant Earthworm|PassionOfTheHeist} about 7 ft. long. Though not initially very threatening, the worm will split whenever it is cut, literally multiplying the challenge.

After the players have faced all their challenges, Joshua will eventually be able to reunite everyone, speaking with the bats to help navigate. This will also allow him to locate the best way to enter the treasury. Once he does, the players will have to find a way to break down the wall without alerting the guards inside. One possible solution is to use the {@item Lantern of Silence|PassionOfTheHeist} while breaking down the wall, which will require a {@dc 13} Strength saving throw.
As the party steps into the treasury, there is a loud crash outside, towards where the front entrance should be. This will become important later when Zoro's other heist is revealed.

data.name: 4. The Heist Part 2
entries: The party's goal for this segment of the heist is to enter the vault, remove its contents, and escape from the treasury. This section of the module will be more open-ended, with players able to explore the area and decide when and how they want to approach each challenge. Josh will only provide suggestions and support to the party in the form of healing. This section is divided into three parts. The first will cover the layout of the treasury and its various security measures. the second will cover how the players will enter the vault. The third section will cover some of the unexpected events that will happen while the party attempts to carry out the heist.

entries.name: The Treasury
entries: The treasury is truly a work of architectural wonder, made up of white marble walls and pillars. A waterfall flows from the top floor to the garden below, teeming with plant life and all the vibrancy of spring. Gold statues and renaissance-style murals fill each room with a sense of sophistication and grandeur. Although completely underground, the building is filled with natural light, as though it was all in the middle of a meadow. There also happen to be a lot of things ready to kill people.

entries.name: Security
entries: {@creature Remoran Soldier|PassionOfTheHeist|Remoran soldiers} patrol the building, often along with {@creature Guard Rabbit|PassionOfTheHeist|guard rabbits} on the lookout. Not only do the guard rabbits have advantage on all perception checks, but they can detect the use of magic within 20ft. The players will be able to tell when the rabbit has picked up on something, as their ears will move much like antennae.

The party will not be able to take on all the security at once, so they must use their items and stealth abilities to move around undetected, picking their battles wisely. If a single player is discovered, this will not typically set off the alarm. The guards will simply try to apprehend them to be interrogated in the office. If multiple are located or if bodies start to pile up, the alarm will be activated, a loud ringing noise coming from seemingly nowhere. The doggie-doors in the lobby will open to unleash the {@creature Attack Lamb|PassionOfTheHeist|attack lambs} who will hunt down the intruders.

entries.name: The Top Floor
entries: The players will begin at the top floor, opening a hole into the wall about 15ft. above the floor. Upon entering the players should now be shown the {@area Top Floor|4.3|x}.

The top floor overlooks the garden down in the lobby, with an artificial river flowing down into a waterfall below. On one side of the room is a massive mural depicting the Remoran conquest of Judrael. On the opposite side a mural depicts what appear to be philosophers at a symposium. One philosopher with broad shoulders and a beard holds up some kind of blue egg towards the sky. This is in fact one of the eggs necessary to open the safe.

The floor is patrolled by 3 {@creature Remoran Soldier|PassionOfTheHeist|Remoran soldiers}. 3 {@creature Guard Rabbit|PassionOfTheHeist|guard rabbits} sit inside the rabbit pen, off-duty but still vigilant. In one corner is the bunk room, where the party will find several bunk beds as well as the {@area Bunk Items|4.4|x}. Under the cushion of one of the benches, there is a small spherical object, which serves as one of the red herrings (see {@area Red Herrings|4.9|x}).

entries.name: Bunk Items
entries: {@item Dipping Stone|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Frosted Blade|PassionOfTheHeist}

entries.name: The Lobby
entries: The players can access the lobby either through the stairs or by dropping down into the garden. When they do, they should be shown the {@area Lobby|4.5|x}. There are 3 {@creature Remoran Soldier|PassionOfTheHeist|Remoran soldiers} in the lobby, each with {@creature Guard Rabbit|PassionOfTheHeist|guard rabbits} on leashes. There are also four doggy doors at the south end of the room, from which the {@creature Attack Lamb|PassionOfTheHeist|attack lambs} will emerge if the alarm is sounded.

entries.name: The Garden
entries: The garden will offer a good opportunity to hide from the security within the mass of flowers and other plant life. It will also contain some things that may be of interest to the players. The yellow egg can be found in the nest of the golden chicken statue in the dirt, while the purple egg can be found underwater at the top of the fountain. There is also a large rose bulb sticking out of the bushes, which serves as one of the red herrings (see {@area Red Herrings|4.9|x}).

entries.name: The Vault
entries: The vault appears as a massive slab of gold-plated metal, forming a mural of entangled flowers and rabbits and baby chicks. There is no breaking the vault; it is indestructible. The vault cannot be teleported into and out of by magical means. The only way to enter the vault without opening the door as intended is to use the {@item Ring of the Second Dimension|PassionOfTheHeist}, which will not allow one to remove its contents, even with the {@item Basket of Holding (X5)|PassionOfTheHeist}.

In front of the vault is a panel with three egg-shaped grooves. The three eggs must be located and placed in these grooves in order for the vault to open. See {@area Finding The Eggs|4.8|x} for further instructions.

entries.name: The Lever
entries: There is a lever on one side of the garden, covered in a jewelencrusted case. The sign next to the lever explains in large letters that it is for emergencies only, and presents an extreme level of danger. Another, much shoddier sign next to that one explains further than no, the lever does not open the vault, Jerry. Make sure the players know that they probably don't want to pull this lever. If it is pulled, it will summon the {@creature The Great Bilby of Eoster|PassionOfTheHeist} (see {@area The Great Bilby of Eoster|4.10|x}).

entries.name: The Back Hall
entries: The back hall can be entered through the lobby, at which point they should be shown the {@area Back Hall|4.6|x}. There is only 1 soldier in the back hall, who is asleep at their desk in the office.

entries.name: Map Statues Size
entries: Note that although the maps are not precisely drawn to scale, the statues should be about the size of a medium creature.

entries.name: The Statues
entries: The statues are not particularly special, but a small sized character will be able to hide in the foliage around their platforms. Additionally, the pink egg is hidden within the lute of the furthest statue.

entries.name: The Departmental Vaults
entries: The eastern wall is lined with small vaults with the names of the different departments of the Remoran administration. These vaults cannot be opened. If a player tries to force one of them open, it quickly becomes red-hot and the player must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 2d6 + 1} fire damage.

entries.name: The Office
entries: Inside the office is a {@creature Remoran Soldier|PassionOfTheHeist} sleeping at the desk. If the party can get around the room without waking them, they will be able to take the {@area Office Items|4.7|x}. The office is the room that individual intruders will be taken to for questioning.

entries.name: Office Items
entries: {@item Scroll of Reverse (1 Use)|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Scroll of Pick Up Four (1 Use)|PassionOfTheHeist}
{@item Handcuffs|PassionOfTheHeist}

entries.name: The Armory
entries: The armory is a fairly small room with a variety of different weapons lining the walls, all showing an immense potential for power. There is what looks like a flamethrower made out of a golden engraving of a dragon. There is a large axe with glowing runes all over the blade. There is heavy armor out of shimmering translucent material. A blade crackles with electricity. A gatling crossbow boasts an impossible rate of fire. This is, of course, a trap.

As soon as a player touches any of these items they will be immediately transported to the elemental plane of geese. They find themselves in a field of grass, surrounded by an endless army of geese harassing them. The ground is covered in droppings as far as the eye can see. The clouds in the sky are nothing more than swarms of geese flying in overlapping Vs. The honking crowds out any other noise, an eternal cacophony of madness.

A door appears a few yards from the player, freestanding in the field. Desperate for a way out, they run towards it, pushing through their feathered assailants as they go. But as soon as they touch the handle, the door shatters into countless small pieces of wood. The pieces soar away in the wind, making an almost flapping motion as they go. The player sinks to their knees in despair, before collapsing completely onto the ground. From up close they can see that the field is not made of grass by millions of small green goose necks, each with heads biting at their skin. The player opens their mouth to scream, but their throat is able only to emit a terrible honk.

So, the player was not actually transported to the plane of geese, but they have been affected by a spell targeting their psyche. After what feels like years of their life, the player finds themselves back in the armory, exactly where they were before. They must immediately succeed on a {@dc 11} Wisdom saving throw or lose their self-control, crying out madly (though not necessarily screaming). Nearby guards will have to roll a perception check to try to hear them.
Until the player's character reunites with Josh, who can remove the affliction, they are now cursed with {@i goose madness}.

entries.name: Goose Madness
entries: Until cured of this affliction, the player will have to attempt a {@dc 14} wisdom saving throw each round of combat or, outside of combat, whenever the DM chooses. On a failed save they must suffer 1 of consequences randomly determined by a D8.

rows: The player makes an involuntary honking noise as they suffer a nervous breakdown and is stunned for 1 turn
The character becomes frightened and must use their action and movement each round to flee from anything that moves quickly or suddenly, flapping their arms as they go.
The character begins babbling about the plane of geese and is incapable of normal speech and spellcasting for 1 turn.
The character experiences vivid hallucinations of geese and is unable to concentrate. They also have disadvantage on ability checks.
The character has an overpowering urge to eat grass, and will only be able to force themselves to take minimal precautions along the way.
The character believes they can fly, and will jump from great heights if that is the most efficient route to get where they want to go.
All voices sound like the honking of geese, and the character is unable to discern audible speech.
The violent urges of the geese overtake the player, and they must make an attack against the closest living creature.

entries: If the player with goose madness is discovered alone, the guards will probably just bring them to the office as they babble to themselves. They will likely complain about having to deal with this sort of thing and say that admin should have splurged for The Unspoken One.

entries.name: The Vault
entries: The ultimate goal of the party is to get into the vault. In order to do so, they must collect the three hidden eggs and place them in the panel in front of the vault.

entries.name: Finding The Eggs
entries: In order to find an egg, a player character must specify the exact location that they are checking in. For example, they cannot simply specify "the lute statue", they must also say that they are looking in the body of the lute. If they want to check a general area for clues, an investigation check may be warranted. The range of their search should determine the DC, but you'll want to keep it fairly high (~17) so that actually guessing the precise location of the egg is typically the better option.

entries.name: The Pink Egg
entries: The pink egg is located inside the lute of the statue at the end of the back hall. The strings of the statue are real, which may act as a clue, but will also require anyone reaching their hand into the lute to succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check to avoid hitting the strings and making noise.

entries.name: The Purple Egg
entries: The purple egg is located at the very top of the fountain, submerged in the water. Players may be able to see this egg from the top floor if they specify they are looking at the fountain and succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. Since the fountain is several feet high, retrieving the egg will likely require climbing out of cover in the garden, and a stealth check may be required depending on the security that is present.

entries.name: The Blue Egg
entries: The blue egg can be seen in the symposium mural, held up by a bearded philosopher in the middle of the scene. The players will have to dive into the mural in order to enter the world of the painting. They will come out on the other side inside the symposium. Behind them is another mural depicting a freezeframe of the treasury a few seconds prior. Those still in the treasury will be able to see the players within the mural, who have become part of the scene.

Once inside the mural, all the characters in the symposium will look at them with a variety of confused and shocked faces. The exception is the man holding the blue egg, who seems to have been expecting this. This is {@creature Aristocles|PassionOfTheHeist}. Aristocles tells the players he will given them the blue egg if they answer his riddle, outlined below.

entries.name: The Riddle
entries: {@b Q:} To leap. Fresh soil. To once again recoil. Always forward, never reverse, and yet always returning to this same verse. What am I?
{@b A:} Spring

Alternatively, a player can choose to fight Aristocles in one-on-one combat. Aristocles is able to create a coliseum, locking him and another player in a world of blurry paint strokes. He will only elect to do this if multiple players try to fight him at once.

entries.name: Red Herrings
entries: In addition to the actual eggs hidden throughout the treasury, there are several red herrings that will lead the players astray.

entries.name: The Rose Bulb
entries: In the garden there is a prominent rose bulb sticking out of the bushes that has yet to bloom. If a player tries to pull it open, they must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 2d6 + 1} poison damage from the toxic cloud that is emitted.

entries.name: The Yellow Egg
entries: A fourth, yellow egg is hidden in the nest of the chicken statue in the garden. This is in fact not one of the eggs that will open the vault, but a chocolate egg wrapped in yellow foil. Whoever is holding the egg must succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check in order to discern that this egg is in fact chocolate. Otherwise, they will not find out until they place it in the panel and promptly melts into a gooey mess. If a player is aware of its true nature, they now have the {@item Chocolate Egg|PassionOfTheHeist} item.

entries.name: Chocolate Egg
entries: {@item Chocolate Egg|PassionOfTheHeist}

entries.name: The Lump
entries: On one of the benches on the top floor there is a lump underneath one of the cushions. A successful {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check will tell a player that the shape is largely spherical (rather than egg shaped). If they lift the cushion, a {@creature Perfectly Spherical Rat|PassionOfTheHeist} will leap out and latch onto their face, requiring a {@dc 11} Strength check to remove. Any attacks against the rat while on the player's face will be at disadvantage or said player will take half of all damage dealt to the rat.

entries.name: Inside The Vault
entries: Once the pink, purple, and blue eggs have all been placed in the panel, the vault will start to open, lifting up like a garage door. This will naturally alert the attention of the nearby security unless they are otherwise distracted.

The vault is quite large, roughly the size of a double garage. Most of the space is taken up by two stacks of gold bars, 20 × 20 × 20ft. Along the walls are various artifacts from different cultures in the surrounding area, encrusted with jewels and shaped out of precious metals. The most prominent is a 10ft. tall statue of a bipedal hare wielding a scimitar, which can be knocked over and into a basket of holding using a {@dc 14} Strength saving throw. The baskets of holding will also come in handy as the players try to grab as many of the gold bars as possible.

Lying behind one of the stacks of gold is a 2ft. fish person surrounded by half-eaten chocolate rabbits and empty jars of multivitamins. A large sack with a dollar sign printed on it sits next to him. This is {@creature Ichthmael|PassionOfTheHeist}. If the party is willing to listen, Ichthmael explains that he was a great burglar, who was the first to successfully break into the Remoran Treasury several months ago. When he entered the vault, however, the guards elected to simply remove one of the eggs from the panel and trap him inside. Ichthmael is willing to join the party if they are willing to let him, and will use his ability to create illusory clones of himself to help them get away.
Once the players have taken as much loot as they can, they will now have to worry about escaping the treasury, either out from where they came from or directly through the front door.

entries.name: Events
entries: As the players are carrying out the heist and searching for the hidden eggs, several events will take place that will complicate their task. These events will typically take place in the order they are described here, but the exact time they will occur should be decided based on what is most narratively fitting. The goal is to increase the chaos without directly negating the party's immediate plans.

entries.name: The Other Heist
entries: As it turns out, Josh is not the only messiah attempting to rob the treasury with his apostles. As the waiter in the tavern suggested, another group has been making similar plans. Another hint is dropped when, as the party enters the treasury, there is a loud crash outside. Though this has no immediate consequences, this comes to a head much later when three figures burst through the front door in the lobby.

Leading the way is a bearded man in white vestments holding what appears to be a bat made out of a bundle of twigs. This is {@creature Zoro|PassionOfTheHeist}. Zoro is followed by the {@creature Zoroastrian Fire Apostle|PassionOfTheHeist} wielding a torch staff and the {@creature Zoroastrian Water Apostle|PassionOfTheHeist} wielding a canoe paddle.

Since their method of entry was not exactly subtle, Zoro and his followers will likely set off the alarm and a fight may break out. If the players are not actively hiding they are liable to get caught in the crossfire. Despite their dramatic introduction, Zoro's crew will try to avoid fighting all of the security at once and will eventually seek to hide and switch to a stealthier approach. They will then try to search for the hidden eggs and get into the vault, just like the party.

Whether Zoro and his crew are friends of foes depend on the circumstances and the attitude of the party. Much like Josh, Zoro is a very friendly person and will be willing to join forces if asked. But if the party is not so trusting or becomes too much of a liability they will also be willing to go it alone and take the loot for themselves. If much of the loot in the vault is destroyed or made inaccessible, perhaps by the Great Bilby, Zoro may decide that there isn't enough to go around and try to take as much as possible for himself and his team.

entries.name: Pontius Pilate
entries: If the alarm has been sounded and the situation has escalated, the governor himself will eventually show up with his elite force of immortals. {@creature Pontius Pilate|PassionOfTheHeist} enters through the front door followed by the {@creature Remoran Rock Immortal|PassionOfTheHeist}, {@creature Remoran Paper Immortal|PassionOfTheHeist}, and {@creature Remoran Scissors Immortal|PassionOfTheHeist}. The immortals are dressed quite similarly to the standard Remoran soldiers but with eagle masks covering their faces. The paper immortal will likely stand out the most with her hang glider.

Pilate is not so much angry as he is disappointed. Never wanting much to do with the party or whatever was going on with them, he is tired of putting up with this and increasingly exasperated as the situation continues to escalate. If the tides of battle turn significantly against him, Pilate is more likely to walk out and quit the governorship than let himself be killed over this whole mess. In that case, any surviving immortals will fight to protect his retreat.

entries.name: The Great Bilby of Eoster
entries: At some point, by someone, the lever in the lobby is going to be pulled. Perhaps it is by one of the soldiers trying to stop the heist(s). Perhaps it is by one of Zoro's apostles who thinks it will provide a welcome distraction for the guards. Perhaps it is one of your players. Either way, when the lever is pulled, a loud nuclear alarm is sounded several times for a period of about 30 seconds. Nothing happens immediately. The length of the delay will depend on the flow of the story, and ideally this will be used to set up the climax. Eventually, however, {@creature The Great Bilby of Eoster|PassionOfTheHeist} will smash through the ceiling and land in the middle of the lobby. The size of a blue whale, this marsupial has glowing red eyes and a blue Roman-style cape pinned to its back. Each step crackles with electricity and raw power.

The Bilby proceeds to wreck a path of destruction throughout the treasury, breaking down the building as it fires its atomic breath. It will focus somewhat on those stealing from the vault, but all will get caught in its path. It cares not for who it obliterates along the way, not the guards, not Zoro, not even Pilate himself. Once the Great Bilby has arrived, everything is a question of survival The party may be able to take it on if they are at full health, but more likely they will need to get out as quickly as possible, whether back through the caves or out through the front entrance (see {@area The Front Entrance|4.11|x}).

entries.name: The Caves
entries: As they are pursued through the caves, the party will have to succeed on several skill checks in order to avoid falling behind and facing the wrath of the bilby. Failing a check will allow the bilby 1 additional attack on the player. All checks and saving throws will be {@dc 14}.

items: A strength saving throw to push through the debris.
An acrobatics check to leap over stones that have fallen in their way.
A survival check to navigate the caves without getting lost.
An investigation check to find a way out of a cavern they are trapped inside.
An athletics check to swim through the water in a flooded segment of the tunnels.

entries.name: The Front Entrance
entries: With Zoro and his crew breaking in through the front of the building, that route is now accessible to the party as a means of escape. for that reason it is necessary to explain the various security measures left over after Zoro's break in.

The front entrance once included a large hallway filled with Remoran soldiers and guard rabbits, with ballista turrets mounted on intervals between statues of famous Remorans. This has all been crushed by the giant boulder that Zoro's apostles rolled into the front of the building.

The hallway also included several archways projecting magical barriers that one must pass through to proceed. These archways were broken by the giant boulder but not completely destroyed. That means that any party member trying to escape must make a choice as they reach each of the barriers. They can attempt to pass through the barrier and suffer the consequences, or they can crawl through the nearby rubble at half speed, granting the bilby 1 additional attack against them. The barriers are as follows, starting from the closest to the lobby.

entries.name: Anti-Magic Barrier
entries: Anyone or any object that passes through this barrier has all of their magical properties and abilities removed for 6 hours. Zoro and his crew originally passed this barrier by crawling through the rubble around it.

entries.name: Anti-Teleportation Barrier
entries: No creature is able to teleport or open a portal past this point. Zoro and his crew originally passed this barrier by not teleporting. This one is a bit of a gimme.

entries.name: Remoran Purity Barrier
entries: This barrier blocks the passage of anyone who doesn't have genuine pride and love for the Remoran Empire in their hearts. Anyone who does not can attempt a {@dc 19} Charisma saving throw to think enough positive thoughts to fool the barrier. Zoro and his crew originally passed this barrier by becoming Remoran history buffs until the cognitive dissonance pushed them to forgive the empire's war crimes.

entries.name: Josh
entries: As the Great Bilby continues to pursue the party, Josh decides to reveal his true nature. He flies up to the bilby, grows fangs, and bites into its neck, mumbling to the party to get away. If the party decides to fight the bilby anyway, a combat will begin with Josh using his vampiric powers to help fight it. Otherwise, as the players continue to flee, they see the bilby growing visibly weaker as it struggles with Josh and they both pass out of sight.

Josh reconvenes with the party later, flying over in bat for them shifting back to human. Though he has suffered several fatal wounds, he was unable to die as the bilby did not use any wooden or silver weapons.

data.name: The End
entries: Two days later, Joshua and the party reconvene with the other apostles at The Grey Goose to celebrate their great victory. Josh gives another speech, this time bringing his own wine to hold up in a chalice. He explains that they must now all spread the story of their exploits to all of the empire, so that the people are aware the Remorans are not invincible. He tells them that by drinking the wine, the holy spirit shall be within them, and it will grant them the power to speak in any tongue. As such, all peoples shall be able to hear of their awesome heist.
To close the story, read the following paragraph, or paraphrase in a way that suits your style.

As you take your first sip, a warm feeling develops deep inside you. Then the world around you begins to blur, eventually melding into bright white light in all directions. You cannot see each other, or anything in the tavern, but you all hear the same voice calling to you.
"With my help, no language shall be beyond your reach."
A massive creature appears before you. It seems to be some kind of owl, but with bright, glowing eyes, and sleek, jade feathers.
"But it will take some practice."
END.
